questions.evidence:
LUNCH MENU: Rice boxes cost fifty dollars each; vegetable wraps cost forty. Every rice box contains chicken. Wraps contain no meat. Orders of four hundred dollars or more receive free delivery. Smaller orders have a thirty-dollar delivery fee, with no other charges.

GROUP LIST: Eight students need lunch. Three do not eat meat; the other five prefer rice boxes but can also eat wraps. The class has four hundred and twenty dollars. Each student needs exactly one meal, and extra food cannot be stored at school.

Ken suggests five rice boxes and three wraps. Ana calculates the food total before adding delivery. Another student suggests eight rice boxes to reach the free-delivery amount, but the group checks the meal requirements before deciding that a lower delivery fee solves everything.

They order Ken's combination and write each student's choice beside their name. The food stand confirms the final amount, including delivery, before accepting payment. Ana saves the message so the class can compare the received meals with what it actually ordered.
